bio_en: Misak Simonian, known as Khmbapet (commander) Misak, was born in Van in 1883 and joined the ARF as a youth, serving as a soldier, agent and courier. In 1904 he went with the courier Poghos to the monastery of St. Thaddeus and carried arms there from Davarlu. In the Armenian-Tatar clashes of 1905 he joined Seydo Poghos's band in Old Nakhichevan and fought in the self-defence of the Armenian village of Khanlakhlar. His later life of wandering and struggle took him through Persia and the volunteer movement, and he died in Iran in 1959.
notes: Compiled from the archive review, 2026-10-12. Confidence: medium. Death year from the 40th-day eulogy (Alik, 23 Aug 1959).
